extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: A benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages, with open-source code and a public leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.citeAs: Muennighoff, Niklas; Tazi, Nouamane; Magne, Loïc; Reimers, Nils. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies 58 datasets from 8 embedding tasks: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. It incorporates existing datasets such as SemEval STS datasets and BEIR, and also includes custom-made datasets for MTEB. New datasets for existing tasks can be benchmarked via a single file specifying the task and a Hugging Face dataset name where the data has been uploaded. Some datasets were created for MTEB using public APIs and available online data, such as arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv APIs, Reddit posts, and StackExchange posts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include existing public benchmark datasets and corpora, including SemEval STS datasets, BEIR datasets, Amazon reviews, Banking77, Emotion, IMDB, MASSIVE, MTOP, Civil Comments, Twitter datasets, BUCC, Tatoeba, AskUbuntu, MIND, SciDocs, StackOverflow, and SummEval. Custom clustering datasets were created for MTEB using public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, and available data from Reddit posts and StackExchange posts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: For medRxiv clustering data, cases were identified between 1/1/2003 and 31/12/2018. No overall benchmark-wide collection timeframe is provided.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For clustering datasets, MTEB defines sentence-to-sentence, paragraph-to-paragraph, and sentence-to-paragraph settings. In ArxivClustering P2P, abstracts are concatenated to titles. For bioRxiv and medRxiv, category labels are used directly; for arXiv, when multiple categories can be given to a paper, only the first one is used. For every clustering dataset, split and strategy, subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels. For retrieval, reranking, STS, pair classification, and summarization, embeddings are compared using cosine similarity or other distance metrics as specified by task.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Task-specific preprocessing includes embedding train and test sets for classification; training logistic regression on train embeddings; embedding texts and applying mini-batch k-means for clustering; computing distances between embedded text pairs for pair classification and STS; embedding queries, references, corpora, and summaries for reranking, retrieval, and summarization. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving it up to models to truncate if necessary. For clustering tasks framed as both S2S and P2P, S2S uses titles only while P2P uses title plus content or abstract.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations come from the original source datasets and include labels such as translations for bitext mining, class labels for classification, duplicate/paraphrase labels for pair classification and reranking, relevance judgments for retrieval and reranking, continuous similarity scores for STS, human-written summaries and human assessments for summarization, and human-assigned paper categories for custom clustering datasets. For custom arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv clustering datasets, cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For pair classification, various distance metrics are evaluated and the best binary threshold is used. For clustering, v-measure is used because it does not depend on cluster label permutation. For summarization, distances from machine summaries to all human summaries are computed and the closest score is kept as the model score. The paper notes that controlling for overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is challenging and these overlaps are ignored in MTEB scores, with the authors believing the effects to be insignificant when enough datasets are averaged.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark aims for reproducibility through versioning at a dataset and software level. JSON files corresponding to all results in the paper have been made available together with the benchmark. The MTEB software is open-source, datasets and leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub, and the authors welcome dataset, task, metric, and leaderboard contributions from the community via pull requests and an automatic submission format.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language is explicitly represented across datasets, with multilingual coverage of 112 languages. Some datasets also involve user-generated text such as customer reviews, online banking queries, tweets, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, and toxic conversation comments.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research and industry applications of text embeddings. The paper discusses that insufficient evaluation can lead to the blind application of models to new use cases in industry.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Task imbalance is identified as a benchmark bias: summarization consists of only a single dataset, so MTEB average scores are biased toward tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering. The paper also notes possible data contamination, for example parts of SciDocsRR likely being included in some models' training data, and states that overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is ignored in MTEB scores. Multilingual coverage is also imbalanced, with retrieval and clustering being English-only.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper lists several limitations: very long document datasets are missing; tasks are imbalanced in number of datasets, biasing average scores toward retrieval, classification and clustering; multilingual coverage is incomplete because retrieval and clustering are English-only; SGPT-BLOOM-7B1-msmarco cannot be comprehensively benchmarked due to lack of multilingual retrieval datasets; MTEB does not contain code datasets; and the benchmark focuses solely on natural language applications, not multimodal downstream uses.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluation and benchmarking of text embedding models across 8 tasks and diverse use cases including clustering, search, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, summarization, classification, and bitext mining. The paper evaluates models primarily on test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO, where the dev split is used following prior work. It also provides baselines, open-source evaluation software, public results JSON files, and a leaderboard for comparing models.
